name: Code-Based Cryptography Assessment
description: Assessment of code-based post-quantum cryptographic schemes, whose security rests on the hardness of decoding random linear codes (the syndrome decoding problem). Covers HQC, selected by NIST in March 2025 as a backup KEM alongside ML-KEM with its standard still in preparation; Classic McEliece, not selected in the NIST round 4 outcome but pursued through ISO/IEC standardisation and favoured for conservative long-term confidentiality; and BIKE. Covers parameter set review, the operational consequences of very large public keys, implementation correctness, constant-time decoding, and the decoding-failure behaviour of quasi-cyclic schemes that enables reaction attacks such as GJS when keys are reused. Because no FIPS standard for a code-based scheme is published, assessments must be explicit about which specification version is in scope.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to code-based cryptography assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands the role of code-based schemes in post-quantum cryptography and how they differ from lattice-based schemes
evidence: Can explain the syndrome decoding problem at a conceptual level and why it is believed quantum-hard
Can name the main code-based candidates (HQC, Classic McEliece, BIKE) and their standardisation status
Understands the key size and ciphertext size trade-off against lattice-based KEMs
Can explain why a second KEM family is wanted alongside ML-KEM

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies code-based deployments and reviews parameter selection under supervision
evidence: Identifies code-based KEM usage in a protocol or product and records the specification version in scope
Reviews parameter set selection against stated security levels under guidance
Uses reference implementations and known-answer test vectors to validate correct operation
Documents the operational impact of public key size on handshakes, certificates and storage
Documents post-quantum findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses code-based cryptography deployments for correctness and security
evidence: Evaluates an HQC or Classic McEliece implementation against its submission specification and test vectors
Assesses parameter selection relative to target security level and deployment constraints, including whether key transmission is feasible on the transport in use
Identifies deviations from specification in key generation, encapsulation or decapsulation that could weaken security
Assesses whether the deployment reuses a static key pair and, for quasi-cyclic schemes with non-zero decoding failure rate, whether that exposes it to reaction attacks
Verifies that decapsulation failure is handled per specification and does not leak through error paths or timing
Produces findings that state the specification version relied upon and the current standardisation status

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex code-based deployment assessments; evaluates implementation side-channel resistance
evidence: Evaluates code-based implementations for timing and power side-channels, particularly in syndrome computation and decoding
Assesses constant-time properties of the decoder and of secret-dependent memory access patterns
Assesses hybrid constructions combining a code-based KEM with a classical or lattice-based KEM, including combiner correctness
Advises on migration where public key size breaks protocol or hardware assumptions
Mentors junior staff on code-based cryptography assessment

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines code-based assessment methodology; recognised authority on code-based post-quantum schemes
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's code-based cryptography assessment methodology
Published research on code-based scheme implementations, decoders or vulnerabilities
Provides expert guidance on code-based scheme selection and parameter choice for long-term confidentiality
Contributes to code-based standardisation efforts or tracks and interprets them for the lab
Trains teams on code-based cryptography internals and assessment approaches

assessment_methods.description: Assess a protocol deployment using a code-based KEM: evaluate parameter selection, verify operation against test vectors, and judge the handling of decapsulation failure
Given a code-based KEM implementation and its specification, identify deviations from the specification and determine whether the decoder is constant-time with respect to the private key

fips.status: No FIPS standard for a code-based scheme is published. HQC was selected on 11 March 2025 as a backup KEM alongside ML-KEM; its draft standard was still unpublished as of October 2026. Classic McEliece and BIKE were not selected in the round 4 outcome.

iso: ISO/IEC standardisation of Classic McEliece in progress
